items.title: Proposition 3.61 · ambient-to-tangent gradient projection

source.anchor: §3.8, Definition3.58 and equations3.36–3.38; Proposition3.61 (3.39), printed42–44 / PDF58–60
source.attribution: Nicolas Boumal. ASTIS attributed restatement. Affine restriction is a prerequisite; sphere projection is a scoped nonlinear application. Neither completes the general embedded-manifold theorem.

items.statement: On a Riemannian submanifold of Euclidean space with the induced metric, the gradient of a smooth function is the tangent-space orthogonal projection of the ambient gradient of any smooth neighborhood extension.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional Euclidean ambient space and embedded submanifold with induced Riemannian metric.
Smooth real-valued f on the manifold and a smooth extension to a neighborhood.

obligations.label: Canonical gradient under linear/affine restriction with inherited metric.
Actual nonlinear tangent/differential and extension-independence adapter.
Smoothness of the resulting manifold gradient field.
Unit-sphere specialization: use the actual manifold differential and inclusion derivative to construct and uniquely characterize its ambient induced-gradient representative.

bindings.boundary: This is the linear/affine restriction prerequisite for Boumal §3.8. Arbitrary embedded-manifold tangent identification, differential restriction, extension semantics and smooth gradient fields remain open; Proposition 3.61 and Chapter 3 are not complete.

assumption_deltas.source: Finite Euclidean ambient and tangent subspaces.
assumption_deltas.lean: Complete real Hilbert E and complete linear subspace K.
assumption_deltas.reason: The pairing mechanism works for complete subspaces; finite-dimensional source instances satisfy completeness. This is not a nonlinear tangent adapter.

assumption_deltas.source: Smooth function and smooth neighborhood extension.
assumption_deltas.lean: Pointwise genuine HasGradientAt for f:E→ℝ; literal affine restriction.
assumption_deltas.reason: One-point differentiability suffices for this library node. The source requires independent nonlinear extension/differential semantics.

assumption_deltas.lean: Inherited inner product on K and gradient typed in K.
assumption_deltas.reason: The chosen subspace metric is exactly inherited. No arbitrary Riemannian metric identification is claimed.

bindings.boundary: Unit-sphere specialization with true Mathlib manifold differential and ambient tangent representation using actual inclusion derivative; pointwise ambient HasGradientAt generalizes smoothness. No general embedded-manifold theorem, chosen default chart metric identification, global smooth field, general neighborhood extension construction or Rayleigh quotient computation. No global Riemannian metric typeclass or smooth-field construction is certified by the pointwise pairing.

assumption_deltas.lean: Actual pointwise ambient HasGradientAt f g; literal restriction of total f.
assumption_deltas.reason: Only the actual derivative at x is used; no smooth extension construction or global smooth-field conclusion.

assumption_deltas.source: General Riemannian submanifold with induced Euclidean metric.
assumption_deltas.lean: Unit sphere with actual Mathlib inclusion differential and ambient tangent-subspace pairing.
assumption_deltas.reason: This source-present sphere specialization explicitly discharges the nonlinear adapter here; it does not stand for all embedded submanifolds or a default chart metric.

assumption_deltas.source: Finite Euclidean space and tangent vector at x.
assumption_deltas.lean: FiniteDimensional real inner-product E, finrank=n+1, x:sphere0E1, candidate z:x⊥ and chart tangent w transported by the true inclusion derivative.
assumption_deltas.reason: Dimension and carrier typing match the sphere application; exact range and differentiability are proof dependencies, not added premises.

chapter_reader.goal: Turn smooth embedded geometry into first-order optimization: identify feasible directions, differentiate an objective along them, and use the induced metric to represent its differential by a gradient.
chapter_reader.source_scope: Boumal Chapter3, §3.4 Definition3.34/(3.27), (3.28), Proposition3.35 and following extension-choice verification; §3.8 Definition3.58, (3.36)–(3.38), Definition3.60 and Proposition3.61; 2023 pre-publication edition, annotations through2026-10-08.

route.title: Feasible directions
route.text: The tangent space describes first-order motion within the embedded manifold. Affine directions are K; for the unit sphere the actual inclusion differential maps Mathlib tangent directions onto the ambient plane x⊥.

route.title: Differentiate along the space
route.text: Local agreement of extensions gives the same derivative on a true feasible-curve velocity. The sphere adapter now composes the actual inclusion differential with the ambient derivative to construct the true restricted manifold differential. General embedded-manifold tangent/differential and representing-curve adapters remain separate.

route.title: Represent by the metric
route.text: For the induced pairing, the gradient is the unique ambient tangent vector representing the differential. The sphere adapter tests every ambient tangent direction through the exact range of the inclusion differential. Changing the metric requires a separate adapter; no default chart inner product is substituted.

route.title: Project the ambient gradient
route.text: Orthogonal projection removes the normal component without changing tangent pairings. The affine lemma supplies the linear restriction prerequisite; the sphere theorem constructs and uniquely characterizes the projection for the actual nonlinear sphere differential.

chapter_reader.boundary: The curve lemma closes the explicit extension-choice proof edge following Proposition3.35; affine restriction supplies a projection prerequisite; the sphere theorem closes the actual induced-gradient characterization for the unit sphere. General embedded-manifold tangent/differential and extension identification, representing-curve independence/linearity, global induced-metric smoothness and smooth gradient fields remain open. These are scoped partial advances, not completion of either proposition or Chapter3.
